actual: the generator is deterministic. Five consecutive runs of one binary over one corpus are byte-identical outside generated_at, and the artifact committed at the branch tip reproduces byte-identically from branch-tip source. There is no HashMap or HashSet anywhere in src/bin/v06_work_inventory.rs or src/rules_core/wiring_class.rs. The real defect is that units[].id was NOT UNIQUE: 38,540 units carried only 38,511 distinct ids because id slugs the corpus key while duplicate_identity de-duplicates on the exact key, and slug() collapses every run of non-alphanumerics to one underscore. 29 ids carried two units each; 27 of those pairs disagreed on wiring_class and exactly 19 disagreed as computed-vs-display, which is the phantom 19-unit computed->display transition the near-miss reported. Both rows are present in EVERY run; an id-keyed consumer keeps one and drops the other, and which one it drops can differ between two snapshots.

caught_by: the count moved at all. The change was supposed to be order hardening with no semantic effect, so a 7-byte output delta was investigated rather than banked: diffed the pre-sort and post-sort runs, found the single unit, opened its corpus record, found no mechanical token, and then enumerated every record in the book whose NAME matches the needle -- two, with different identities.
gap: equipment_id_resolve's first pass tested the KEY: token alone, so a needle naming a KEY-less record fell through to a bare-name pass that is first-match-wins over the corpus in read_dir order. Nothing asserted that a needle resolves to the record whose corpus identity it is, and nothing asserted resolution is independent of corpus order. 38 equipment names across CRB/ACG/ARG were decided by scan order this way; Potion is the widest, with general/potion.json against fifty-odd Potion of.../Oil of... magic items that all display as Potion.
gate: manual before/after byte-diff of the generator output, then corpus-record inspection
summary: declined a +1 grounded that sorting the corpus scan produced: the promoted item has no mechanical token and the magnitude belonged to a name twin. Fixed the resolver to match corpus identity first, which keeps the unit at ingested-magnitude by rule instead of by luck of filesystem ordering, and leaves the generator's output byte-identical to the committed artifact.
